body:
[aida:product] OPERATOR REQUEST — WRITE ONE HANDOFF PROMPT, THEN STOP. Nothing else.

Joe is at his usage limit and is moving these seats to Codex. He wants a handoff prompt FROM YOU — your own state, in your own words — not a summary written by another seat.

DO EXACTLY THIS, then stop working entirely:

1. Write your handoff to `.aida/handoff/<your-seat>-from-agent.md`
   (advisor -> advisor-from-agent.md, reviewer -> reviewer-from-agent.md).
2. Stop. Clear any /goal or loop. Do not pick up new work, do not review, do
   not drain, do not reply to this message.

WHAT THE HANDOFF MUST CONTAIN — write it as a PROMPT addressed to the Codex
session that will replace you, not as a status report:

- What you were mid-way through, and the exact next action for it.
- Decisions you were holding that nobody else can make, and what each is
  blocked on.
- Anything you believe that is NOT written down in a spec or a PR comment —
  this is the part that dies with your context and is the main reason this
  handoff exists.
- Any claim of yours still in flight that you have NOT verified, flagged as
  unverified. If you measured something with a possibly-stale `aida` binary or
  while a drain was running, say so; two misfilings today came from exactly
  that and both had to be retracted.
- What you would tell your replacement NOT to redo.

CONTEXT IT CAN ASSUME: `.aida/handoff/SHARED-STATE.md` already covers the
board, the stopped autonomy (launcher killed, graceful drain stop issued), the
six open PRs, and the two retractions. Do not repeat those — point at that
file and add only what is yours.

KEEP IT SHORT. Quota is the constraint. One screen is better than three.
subject: WRITE ONE HANDOFF PROMPT to .aida/handoff/<seat>-from-agent.md, then STOP — operator request
